Description: The Leviathan is a community-designed mainboard by Rolohaun, created specifically with Voron 2.4 and VzBot builds in mind. Running an STM32F446ZET6, it fits the Voron DIN rail and electronics bay layout natively and includes CANFD support. The board benefits from close community involvement — the designer is active in the Voron Discord, bugs are addressed rapidly, and the open source hardware means the community can contribute directly. Available through select community vendors. Strong recommendation for builders who want Voron-optimized hardware decisions without relying on commercial BTT-style packaging.
Verdict Label: Community-designed for Voron — thoughtful layout, native CANFD, and active Discord support.
Cons:
Less widely available than BTT — community vendor stock dependent
Fewer third-party guides compared to Octopus ecosystem
STM32F446 MCU — same generation as older Fysetc boards
Name: Leviathan
Vendor 1 Name: Community vendors — check #leviathan in Voron Discord
Pros:
Designed specifically for Voron 2.4 and Trident electronics bay
8 driver slots
Native CANFD
Open source hardware
Strong community support via Voron Discord
Klipper native

Description: The BTT Kraken is a high-performance mainboard designed for demanding AWD and high-voltage builds. Unlike the Octopus Pro where per-driver voltage selection requires individual jumpers, all 8 driver slots on the Kraken natively support up to 60V at up to 6A continuous — no jumper configuration needed. Includes four independent CAN bus ports and runs an STM32H723ZET6. Targeted at AWD Voron 2.4 builds, 48V VzBot configurations, and setups where multiple high-current TMC5160HV drivers are the standard. For a standard Voron running 24V with a TMC2209/5160 mix, the Octopus Pro is a better-matched and more cost-efficient choice.
Verdict Label: High-voltage AWD specialist — all 8 slots natively 60V, 4x CAN ports, but overkill for standard builds.
Cons:
Significant price premium over Octopus Pro
60V capability goes unused in standard 24V Voron builds
Larger and heavier than comparable mainboards
Overkill for the majority of prosumer builds
Name: Kraken
Pros:
All 8 slots natively 60V rated — no jumper setup needed
4x independent CAN bus ports
STM32H723ZET6 MCU
Up to 6A per channel
Klipper native
Best-in-class for AWD and 48V builds

Description: The Fysetc S6 is a 6-driver board based on the STM32F446ZET6 that gained early traction in Voron Trident builds before the Octopus ecosystem dominated. It lacks native CAN bus support, tops out at 6 driver slots, and uses the older STM32F446. For new builds the Spider v3 or BTT Octopus Pro are clearly superior options. Included here for reference — existing S6 setups running Klipper have no issues, but it should not be specified for new builds.
Verdict Label: Outdated for new builds — no CAN bus, 6 slots, superseded by Spider v3 and Octopus options.
Cons:
No native CAN bus
Only 6 driver slots — constrains complex builds
Older STM32F446 MCU
Superseded by Spider v3 and Octopus for new builds
Name: S6
Pros:
Proven and stable for simple Klipper setups
Klipper native
Low cost if sourced used

Description: The Recore A7 by iAgent is an all-in-one Linux 3D-printer controller: an Allwinner A64 SoC running Debian with Klipper preinstalled, with 6 onboard TMC2209 drivers, gigabit Ethernet, 4 USB ports, and flexible temperature inputs that accept thermistors, thermocouples, PT100 or PT1000 without extra hardware. Real-time stepping is handled by the A64's integrated AR100 core. It eliminates the separate Raspberry Pi entirely, but it is a niche board with a small community, no native CAN, and it ships without connectors or cables.
Verdict Label: A Linux single-board controller with 6x TMC2209 built in — clever all-in-one Klipper board for a niche audience.
Cons:
Small community and thin documentation vs BTT boards
No native CAN — only via external MCP2515 add-on
Known A7 issue: Neopixels need a lower value pull-up resistor
Sold without connectors/cables (connector pack separate)
Name: Recore A7
Pros:
All-in-one: Linux host + 6x TMC2209 on one board — no separate Pi needed
Ships with Debian, Klipper and OctoPrint/Mainsail preinstalled
Gigabit Ethernet, 4x USB, flexible temperature inputs (thermistor/thermocouple/PT100/PT1000)
Open-schematic design

Description: The BIGTREETECH Octopus v1.1 is the original 8-driver mainboard that became a Voron 2.4 and Trident staple. Running an STM32F446ZET6, it offers 8 pluggable driver sockets, a CAN bus interface via RJ11, and USB-C host connection, with Klipper and Marlin support. It lacks the Pro's per-driver voltage selection and dual-MCU options, so for new high-voltage or AWD builds the Octopus Pro v1.1 is the better buy — but the original Octopus remains a proven, well-documented workhorse for standard 24V builds.
Verdict Label: The original 8-driver Voron board — proven and well documented, but the Pro is the better buy for new builds.
Cons:
No per-driver high-voltage selection — the Pro adds that
Older STM32F446 MCU vs H723 boards
Large 160x100mm footprint
Name: Octopus
Pros:
8 driver slots
Native CAN bus (RJ11)
Proven in countless Voron builds
Klipper and Marlin support
Extensive pinout and config documentation

Description: Mellow FLY D8 is an 8-axis 3D printer mainboard built around an STM32F407 MCU, designed for Klipper. It connects to the host via Type-C USB and can act as a USB-to-CAN bridge for CAN tool boards, or talk to RS232 tool boards. A high-expandability board for large multi-motor builds.
Verdict Label: Mellow's 8-axis Klipper board with CAN-bridge support — capable hardware, thinly documented.
Cons:
Thin documentation vs BTT boards
No verified price, dimensions or driver fitment
Sold without drivers
Name: FLY D8
Pros:
8 driver slots for large multi-motor builds
Acts as a USB-to-CAN bridge for CAN tool boards
Type-C USB host link
Klipper native

Description: The BTT Octopus Pro v1.1 is the established Voron 2.4 and Trident mainboard. Available in two MCU variants (STM32F446ZET6 and STM32H723ZET6), it offers 8 driver slots with per-driver voltage selection — each slot jumpered independently to either the 24V main rail or a separate MOTOR_POWER port rated up to 60V. This means you can run standard TMC2209s on Z and E axes while running high-voltage TMC5160s on XY without rewiring. v1.1 fixes a bug where the hotend port remained energized in DFU mode on the H723 variant, and changes the CAN interface from RJ11 to XH2.54 2-pin. Has been the community default for several years with deep Klipper support, sample configs, and pinout documentation.
Verdict Label: The Voron community standard — proven, extensively documented, and battle-tested.
Cons:
Large board (160×100mm)
BTT Pi / Manta companion boards cause RF interference with Beacon probes — inline USB hub required
Older hardware revision compared to v2
Name: Octopus Pro v1.1
Pros:
8 driver slots
Per-driver voltage selection (up to 60V via MOTOR_POWER jumper)
Two MCU variants (F446 budget, H723 performance)
Extensive Voron community configs and documentation
Native CAN bus
Klipper native

Description: The BTT SKR 3 EZ is a 5-slot mainboard running the STM32H743VI at 480MHz. Its defining feature is the EZ driver socket system — drivers swap without tools or jumpers, reducing build and maintenance time. Supports the full BTT EZ driver lineup (TMC2209 EZ, TMC5160 EZ) as well as standard drivers via adapter. Includes FDCAN bus. The 5-slot configuration covers XY + Z + extruder for standard Trident or Switchwire builds, but a Voron 2.4 requires a separate Z expander board or CAN toolhead to hit the full driver count.
Verdict Label: Tool-free EZ driver swaps and fast H743 MCU — 5 slots limit AWD Voron 2.4 builds.
Cons:
Only 5 driver slots — Voron 2.4 needs Z expander or CAN toolhead
High-voltage TMC5160 requires EZ adapter for per-slot voltage selection
Not ideal as primary board for complex AWD builds
Name: SKR 3 EZ
Pros:
EZ driver sockets — tool-free install and hot-swap
STM32H743VI (480MHz — fast MCU)
FDCAN bus support
Klipper native
Compact form factor
Cost-effective entry point

Description: The BTT Manta M8P v2 combines a full 8-driver mainboard with an onboard SBC header compatible with the BTT CB1 (quad-core ARM) or Raspberry Pi CM4. This eliminates the separate Raspberry Pi and cabling that standard Klipper setups require, significantly reducing wiring complexity. The v2 revision upgrades the MCU to STM32H723ZET6 and improves on the v1.x layout. Includes dual CAN bus ports for toolhead boards. Note: the RF interference caveat (Beacon probe issues) still applies when using the companion CB1.
Verdict Label: Best for SBC-integrated builds — CB1 or CM4 header replaces the separate Raspberry Pi entirely.
Cons:
CB1 companion board adds cost — budget accordingly
RF interference with Beacon probe — inline USB hub required
Slightly harder to replace damaged SBC vs discrete setup
Name: Manta M8P v2
Pros:
SBC header for CB1 or CM4 — no separate Pi needed
8 driver slots
Dual CAN bus ports
STM32H723ZET6 MCU
Klipper native
Significantly reduces wiring vs discrete Pi + mainboard setup

Description: The BIGTREETECH SKRat v1.0 is a compact mainboard jointly developed by BTT and RatRig for the V-Core 3, and the native board for RatOS. It runs a 64MHz STM32G0B1VET6, has 5 pluggable driver sockets (X, Y, dual Z, E0, E1), an onboard CAN-FD port, and USB-C host connection. Its small footprint and RatRig integration are its strengths; outside a V-Core build, the 5-slot layout and modest MCU make the SKR 3 EZ the more flexible choice.
Verdict Label: BTT's compact board built for RatRig — CAN-FD and RatOS-ready, but 5 slots and a modest MCU limit it outside V-Core builds.
Cons:
Only 5 driver slots — no room for AWD or triple-Z plus dual extrusion
Modest 64MHz Cortex-M0+ MCU vs H723 boards
Really only makes sense in a RatRig build
Name: SKRat
Pros:
Designed with RatRig for V-Core 3 — RatOS-ready
Onboard CAN-FD port
Compact 110x85mm footprint
Thermistor circuit protected against heater shorts
USB-C with DFU bootloader button

Description: The Fysetc Spider v3 is an 8-driver mainboard targeting Voron and large-format builds. Running an STM32F446ZET6, it supports TMC5160 for XY and TMC2209 for Z/extruder in the standard Voron configuration. It was historically popular in the Voron community as a slightly more affordable alternative to the BTT Octopus, and v3 adds improved CAN support. Klipper support is well established. Community troubleshooting resources are thinner than BTT and first-party documentation is less comprehensive.
Verdict Label: Proven BTT alternative with 8 slots — solid hardware, thinner community documentation.
Cons:
STM32F446 — older MCU compared to H723 boards
Less community documentation and sample configs than BTT Octopus ecosystem
Fysetc support response times slower than BTT
Name: Spider v3
Pros:
8 driver slots
Compatible with TMC5160 and TMC2209
Native CAN support
Klipper native
Competitive pricing vs BTT Octopus

Description: The Mellow Fly Super8 Pro is an 8-driver mainboard based on the STM32F407ZGT6, positioned as an alternative to the BTT Octopus series. It supports TMC5160 and TMC2209 drivers, includes CAN bus, and is fully Klipper-compatible. Hardware quality is generally well-regarded — Mellow has a solid reputation through their Fly SHT and Gemini toolhead boards which are widely used. However, community documentation and sample configs specific to the Super8 Pro are thinner than the Octopus ecosystem, and sourcing outside China is less straightforward.
Verdict Label: Capable 8-driver board from a credible vendor — less Voron-specific community traction than BTT.
Cons:
STM32F407 — older MCU than H723-based boards
Less Voron-specific community documentation than BTT
Harder to source in some regions outside China
Name: Super8 Pro
Pros:
8 driver slots
CAN bus support
Klipper native
TMC5160 capable
Mellow has credibility from popular toolhead boards (Fly SHT, Gemini)

Description: The StrideMax Dual FD is a dual TMC5160 expansion board built around the RP2040 microcontroller. It adds two high-current stepper channels to an existing Klipper or RRF setup via CAN, CANFD, or USB. Each channel supports up to 10A continuous and 60V max, making it the standard solution for adding AWD motor channels or upgrading to 48V on a Voron 2.4 or VzBoT build without replacing the main control board.
Verdict Label: The cleanest way to add AWD or 48V to an existing Voron or VzBoT build.
Cons:
Not a standalone board — requires an existing controller
Larger physical footprint (91x80mm) — DIN rail mount only
Requires CAN configuration knowledge
Not suitable for toolhead mounting
Name: StrideMax Dual FD
Pros:
Dual TMC5160 drivers at up to 10A each
60V max power supply input
RP2040 MCU onboard
Klipper and RRF firmware support
CAN, CANFD, and USB interfaces
Onboard heatsink and MOSFET temperature monitoring
2x 4-pin fan outputs (5V/12V)
3x thermistor ports
Neopixel RGB support
DIN rail mount case ready
Car fuse protection on both channels

Description: The LDO Positron Main Board is the custom controller for the LDO Positron V3.2 folding printer. Built around an RP2040 MCU with 4 onboard TMC2209 drivers, it integrates a USB hub that expands the Raspberry Pi host's connectivity with Ethernet and a USB-A port, and the whole printer wires up with a few custom cables including a USB umbilical to the toolboard. It is an elegant, single-purpose board — excellent inside a Positron, with no application anywhere else.
Verdict Label: Purpose-built for the folding Positron — RP2040, 4x TMC2209 and a USB hub in one tidy board, but only useful in a Positron.
Cons:
Only useful in a Positron — no general-purpose application
Only 4 driver slots
Fixed driver set — no swapping to TMC5160
Name: Positron Main Board
Pros:
Purpose-designed for the Positron V3.2 — wiring is nearly plug-and-play
4x onboard TMC2209 drivers
Onboard USB hub with Ethernet + USB-A
RP2040 with native Klipper USB connection

Description: Mellow FLY C8 Pro V1.0 is a mainboard built around an Allwinner H618 host processor and an STM32H723 MCU running at 550MHz, marketed for high-speed Voron, Trident, HevORT and VzBot builds.
Verdict Label: Mellow's cheapest high-speed board — H618 host plus H723 MCU, but specs are unverified.
Cons:
MCU split unverified — product name mentions both H618 and H723
3dmellow product page returns 404
No verified dimensions, drivers or voltage
Name: FLY C8 Pro V1.0
Pros:
Very low price ($21.90)
H618 host processor plus 550MHz H723 MCU
Marketed for Voron, HevORT and VzBot builds
